seed: Objects of type `counter` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [] show mixed outcomes: pixels,w x3, no_change x2. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Player 5x5 ring (9, centre 5) steps 6 cells; a move succeeds iff the dest box is all floor 5, or it holds the plate centre (topmost 3x3 of rope 8).
Body (player/ghost) covering the plate pushes the door block (arm rows +-3, 6 cols from the arm start) 6 toward the line column; release shifts it back.
The 'counter A1 mixed' hypothesis = call parity: counter row 63 turns the rightmost unspent cell colour 1 on every other call, n//2+1 cells spent after call n; parity hidden and continuity-gated (fallback n=2*ones-1).
A5 off spawn toggles ghost mode: first call records the trail [level start, spawn] and respawns, ghost colour 2 trails the player 2 moves behind (hidden while on the player); second call clears. A5 on spawn is a no-op.
HUD: ghost mode draws a colour-2 ring at (1,1) and shifts the player ring/bar to x5; unconfirmed: actions 7 and clicks (unobserved), goal/chamber completion.
